verdicts.evidence: Sympy confirms the identity p·(1−α′)=1−α exactly across a 26-cell grid (max deviation 0.0), and Monte Carlo on Gaussian-mixture data (20 seeds, n=2000) shows PT coverage ≥ nominal−2·SEM and PT length < VCP length in all tested cells; mutation tests confirm the α′ adjustment carries coverage and that length gain is conditional on misspecification as the paper states.

All 16 swept configurations yield PT shorter than VCP with coverage 0.898–0.903; the closest configuration reproduces VCP 22.837±0.058 (paper 22.894±0.138) and PT 22.489±0.063 (paper 22.614±0.254), both within the paper's own standard errors, with the specification discrepancy (μ=20 as separation vs component mean) documented.

Only 6 of 10 datasets were attempted; all three MEPS datasets and star are missing due to gated downloads, so the literal '9 of 10' count cannot be confirmed or refuted. On the 6 attempted datasets, 4 show PT shorter with coverage within 0.02 of nominal, but the claim's core quantitative statement remains unaddressed.

Sympy returns Var = p(1−p)L² matching Proposition 2 exactly, and Monte Carlo over 35 cells (5 seeds × 9 p-values, 500 test points × 400 runs) matches the closed form within 2.47% worst case with IS strictly positive (minimum 4.96); the p=1 mutation drops IS to ≈0, confirming the instability arises from PT randomization.

With σ̂(x)∈{ε,1} drawn as {1−p,p}, localized CP intervals are structurally identical to PT (Eq 2) with per-point length differences ≤0.403 out of ≈22, shorter than VCP on all 40 cells, and IS≥10.08 in every cell; the deterministic σ̂≡1 mutation collapses to VCP with IS≈0, confirming the flag fires on the randomness.

overall: The logbook provides strong symbolic and Monte-Carlo evidence with mutation tests for the theoretical claims (1, 4, 5) and a faithful reproduction of the synthetic Table 1 numbers (claim 2). Claim 3 is honestly blocked: 4 of 10 real-world datasets, including all MEPS datasets named in the claim, were not obtained, leaving the '9 of 10' count unverifiable.
